claim: The game database format (magic GADB) is only partly understood publicly: header, a string table and hashed string pointers are mapped, while record blocks remain 'unknown' and use hardcoded file offsets.
evidence: gamedb.hexpat names fields unknownBlock/unknownChunk and pins chunks at fixed offsets.
game_build_compatibility: UNKNOWN; fixed offsets are tied to one game.gamedb sample of unstated version.
verification_method: Read the pattern files. The SCRI (scripts) pattern only maps a header plus an opaque code blob; strdb maps a hash->offset index with UTF-16 strings.
limitations: Nothing public explains how gamedb records map to Nemesis/orc/mission data; script bytecode format is unknown.
next_experiment: Extract game.gamedb from our build, verify the header layout, and diff string tables for names like Faction/Nemesis to locate relevant records.
